name: RequestShape
purpose: Capture a request's resiliency context (priority class, deadline, idempotency key, retry-count-so-far) in a single immutable record propagated across boundaries.
api_signature:
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Protocol, Literal

Priority = Literal['critical', 'normal', 'sheddable_plus', 'sheddable']

class RequestShape(Protocol):
    request_id: str
    priority: Priority
    deadline_ns: int
    idempotency_key: str | None
    attempt: int
    origin: str
    def to_headers(self) -> dict[str, str]: ...
    @classmethod
    def from_headers(cls, headers: dict[str, str]) -> 'RequestShape': ...
invariants: Fields on a RequestShape instance MUST be immutable after construction; in-place mutation is FORBIDDEN.
A request without an explicit priority SHALL default to normal and NEVER silently to critical.
The attempt counter MUST monotonically increase; a decrement CANNOT occur and breaks retry accounting.
to_headers and from_headers SHALL be mutual inverses on the defined fields, round-tripping without loss.
An idempotency_key once set MUST NEVER be altered across retries of the same logical request.
extension_contract: Adopters register a HeaderAdapter per transport (HTTP, gRPC metadata, queue message attributes) and a PriorityPolicy hook that derives priority from authenticated principal, route, or tenant tier; the wire format is versioned so unknown fields are preserved and not dropped.

why_essential: Resiliency decisions depend on metadata that is easy to lose across hops; a single immutable record that survives transport boundaries turns scattered headers into a contract every primitive can rely on.
alternatives_considered: Ad-hoc headers per client: diverge in naming and CANNOT be validated end to end.
Thread-local storage only: breaks across async boundaries and worker processes.
Rebuild context per layer: wastes CPU and NEVER preserves idempotency keys reliably.
